nodes.name: Sunlight and heat
nodes.desc: Strong sun and high temperatures drive the desert, drying the ground and limiting growth to winter and spring.

nodes.name: Winter rain and rain shadow
nodes.desc: Rain falls mostly in winter and drops steeply from the Judean hills to the Dead Sea side, a rain shadow effect that makes the eastern slopes desert.

nodes.name: Perennial springs
nodes.desc: Springs such as Ein Prat, Ein Mabuah and Ein Qelt keep Wadi Qelt flowing in places and draw wildlife.

nodes.name: Desert soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Thin rocky soils hold the minerals and organic matter that annual plants use after winter rains.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the thin desert soil.

nodes.name: Wild oat
nodes.desc: A wild annual grass of the Mediterranean and steppe zones that sprouts after winter rain and feeds grazers and seed eaters.

nodes.name: Shrubby orache
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant evergreen shrub of dry, saline ground that provides browse in arid areas.

nodes.name: Common fig
nodes.desc: A fruit tree that grows wild on rocky slopes and near water; its fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Mountain gazelle
nodes.desc: A graceful gazelle of hills and wadis in the Levant that grazes and browses on grasses, herbs and shrubs; it is the most recorded large mammal near the site.

nodes.name: Nubian ibex
nodes.desc: A wild goat of the cliffs that feeds mainly on grasses and leaves; it is common along the Dead Sea cliffs and in the Judean Desert.

nodes.name: Rock hyrax
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling herbivore of the cliffs and wadi walls that lives in colonies and eats plant matter.

nodes.name: Cape hare
nodes.desc: A grass and herb eater of open ground, and a regular prey of foxes, jackals and eagles.

nodes.name: Spiny mouse
nodes.desc: A rocky-desert rodent that eats seeds and small invertebrates and is prey for foxes and owls.

nodes.name: Chukar
nodes.desc: A ground-dwelling partridge of rocky slopes that eats seeds and shoots; it is a staple prey of eagles and foxes.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: An adaptable small predator and scavenger that eats hares, birds, rodents, reptiles and fruit such as figs.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that takes small prey and fruit and scavenges carrion around wadis and settlements.

nodes.name: Striped hyena
nodes.desc: A nocturnal scavenger of desert and rocky hills that feeds mostly on carrion, with some small prey.

nodes.name: Griffon vulture
nodes.desc: A large scavenging bird that breeds on cliffs and feeds on carcasses; it is noted as a breeding species of Wadi Qelt.

nodes.name: Arabian wolf
nodes.desc: A small desert wolf that hunts gazelles, ibex and hares and scavenges; it is among the region top predators now that leopards have gone.

nodes.name: Bonelli's eagle
nodes.desc: A cliff-nesting eagle recorded at Wadi Qelt that hunts partridges, hares and other medium-sized prey.
